vga.citation: Wikipedia contributors, Mode 13h (read 10 October 2026); WHATVGA notes (author and date not stated), hosted at sites.cs.ucsb.edu.
claims: Mode 13h: 320 x 200 pixels, one byte per pixel, introduced in 1987 with the IBM PS/2; the DAC has 256 entries of 18 bits, 6 bits per basic colour, allowing 256 colours out of 256K.
vga.does_not_prove: IBM's own specification wording; the IBM VGA Technical Reference was not read. 262,144 is the arithmetic 2^18.

abrash.short: Abrash, Graphics Programming Black Book, ch. 34
abrash.citation: Abrash, M. Graphics Programming Black Book, chapter 34.
claims: The VGA DAC uses 6 significant bits per colour component; the upper two bits of each byte are not significant.
abrash.quote: upper two bits of each byte aren't significant

heckbert1982.citation: Heckbert, P. (1982). Color image quantization for frame buffer display. Computer Graphics 16(3), 297-307 (SIGGRAPH '82). doi:10.1145/800064.801294.
claims: Images can be quantized to 8 or fewer bits per pixel with little subjective degradation.
Median cut: each colormap entry should represent an equal number of pixels; boxes are split at the median along their longest dimension until K boxes exist.
heckbert1982.does_not_prove: That median cut is optimal, or any measured error figure.

bayer1973.citation: Bayer, B. E. (1973). An optimum method for two-level rendition of continuous-tone pictures. IEEE International Conference on Communications, vol. 1. Read through Bouman (2013).
claims: Ordered dither compares each pixel with a threshold from a recursively built index matrix tiled over the image.
bayer1973.does_not_prove: Bayer's own optimality criterion or wording; the page range is unverified.

bouman2013.citation: Bouman, C. A. (2013). Digital Halftoning. ECE637 lecture notes, Purdue University, 29 January 2013.
claims: Bayer's index matrix can be defined recursively; the threshold matrix is T = 255 (I + 0.5) / N^2; an 8 x 8 screen gives only 65 grey levels.

floyd-steinberg.citation: Floyd, R. W., and Steinberg, L. An adaptive algorithm for spatial grey scale. Cited as Proc. SID 17(2), 75-77 (1976) by Ostromoukhov 2001 and Bouman 2013, and as SID 75 Int. Symp. Dig. Tech. Papers (1975), 36 by Heckbert 1982.
claims: Error diffusion with weights 7/16, 3/16, 5/16 and 1/16 to the unprocessed neighbours.
floyd-steinberg.does_not_prove: The original paper's wording or how the weights were chosen; year and venue are cited two ways.

ostromoukhov2001.citation: Ostromoukhov, V. (2001). A simple and efficient error-diffusion algorithm. SIGGRAPH 2001.
claims: Gives the Floyd and Steinberg weights and their placement: 7/16 ahead, 3/16 below-behind, 5/16 below, 1/16 below-ahead.

ulichney1993.citation: Ulichney, R. A. (1993). Void-and-cluster method for dither array generation. Proc. SPIE 1913, 332-343. doi:10.1117/12.152707.
claims: The void-and-cluster method generates dither arrays (the film shows raw-native's own mask, built from this paper).
ulichney1993.does_not_prove: Any blue-noise property; the property shown is raw-native's own test (low-frequency power under 0.2 of high-frequency power).

oklab2020.citation: Ottosson, B. (23 December 2020). A perceptual color space for image processing.
claims: Oklab is designed to predict perceived lightness, chroma and hue, so blends give even transitions.
oklab2020.quote: Blending two colors should result in even transitions.
oklab2020.does_not_prove: That Euclidean distance in Oklab equals perceived colour difference.

rn-dither.citation: HarperZ9/raw-native web/shaders/dither/, web/shaders/reference/retro-dither.mjs and retro-palettes.mjs, evidence/shaders-dither-exhaustive-swiftshader.json, main ba9fb0f.
claims: GPU modes none, bayer2, bayer4, bayer8, noise and blue; picks in OKLab between the two palette colours that bracket the pixel.
16,777,216 colours, 0 mismatches between GPU and CPU, for pico8 with bayer8 and ega with noise; a local run, not part of CI.
A 64 x 64 void-and-cluster mask written from Ulichney 1993; its test asserts low-frequency power under 0.2 of high-frequency power.
rn-dither.quote: local run; not part of CI
rn-dither.does_not_prove: Results for other palette and mode pairs; error diffusion is CPU only and clamps error at 0.5 per channel.

brender-pal.citation: HarperZ9/brender-archival README (rung: File-texture sampling) and modern/viewer/brview_scenes.c load_texture, main 5e02174.
claims: Period .pix textures are 8-bit indices resolved through a 256-entry palette (std.pal when the texture carries none).
brender-pal.does_not_prove: How every 1998 BRender title stored textures.

rosewood-texel.short: BRender 1.3.2 data files, rosewood.pix and std.pal
rosewood-texel.citation: BRender 1.3.2 dat/rosewood.pix (256 x 256 INDEX_8, no palette of its own) and dat/std.pal (256 entries), from foone/BRender-v1.3.2 d88d0ed, looked up as modern/viewer/brview_scenes.c load_texture does.
claims: The 8 x 8 patch of rosewood.pix from texel (124, 124) holds the indices drawn on screen; the texel at (128, 128) holds index 170, and std.pal entry 170 is RGB 99, 24, 24.
rosewood-texel.does_not_prove: How any 1998 title used this texture; the patch shows the lookup, nothing about the art.
rosewood-texel.added: by the film scene-code agent on 14 October 2026 for shot 8.2, pending the author's review; values in scene/rosewood.json, file hashes checked
